incidents.victim: Kyiv Independent (Ukrainian news outlet)
incidents.vector: Hackers gained access to the outlet's website content management system and newsletter-distribution service.
incidents.impact: Attackers published false messages and emailed fabricated nuclear-strike warnings to subscribers in Russian and English; donor and payment data were not affected.

incidents.victim: Crédit Mutuel Arkéa (French bank)
incidents.vector: Attackers compromised a third-party service provider's platform to gain direct access to the bank's own account and initiate fraudulent transfers over several days.
incidents.impact: An estimated $133 million was moved out and partly laundered through cryptocurrency exchanges; customer accounts were unaffected and some assets have been frozen.

incidents.victim: Li Auto electric-vehicle owners in Russia
incidents.vector: Attackers exploit leaked vehicle ID numbers and expired Chinese eSender eSIM numbers to re-register Li Auto master vehicle accounts, generating a new digital key.
incidents.impact: At least 20 confirmed owners (likely more) have had their cars remotely locked and been extorted for roughly $500-600 to regain access; this is the second such wave since July 2025.

incidents.victim: European supermarket and food-supply chains (incl. UK meat suppliers, Ahold Delhaize stores)
incidents.vector: Exploitation of authentication-bypass vulnerabilities in internet-exposed Copeland XWEB refrigeration/freezer supervisory controllers.
incidents.impact: Attackers remotely forced freezers and refrigerators into defrost mode (up to 50°C/122°F) at sites across 12+ European countries, spoiling stock; UK's NCSC called national impact 'minimal' but affected businesses faced significant losses.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian government agencies, judicial institutions, defense organizations, and a foreign military-aid transportation hub
incidents.vector: Phishing emails with malicious attachments disguised as official fine or tax notices deliver the 'BeautyStealer' info-stealer and a reverse-shell tool; recent campaigns exploit a patched WinRAR flaw (CVE-2025-8088).
incidents.impact: The group has stolen credentials, VPN configurations and documents tied to war-crimes investigations, airstrike-damage assessments and military aid logistics since at least February 2025.

incidents.victim: German federal lawmakers and ministry staff
incidents.vector: Mercenary/commercial spyware delivered to targets' devices; Apple's threat-notification system flagged the targeting.
incidents.impact: Germany's cybersecurity agency BSI confirmed multiple Parliament members and staff, including some of Chancellor Merz's staff, were targeted for surveillance.

incidents.victim: U.S. Government (National Reconnaissance Office, State Department, Department of Justice)
incidents.attacker: Foreign state intelligence service — Ethiopia (insider espionage)
incidents.vector: A former U.S. government IT contractor with Top Secret/SCI access used administrator privileges to remove classified documents and transmit them to Ethiopian government officials over more than two years.
incidents.impact: Classified national defense information was reportedly used by Ethiopian officials in military operations against paramilitary groups; the contractor pleaded guilty to conspiracy to transmit national defense information to a foreign government and faces 10-22 years in prison.

incidents.victim: BTCPay Server operators running version 2.4.1 or earlier
incidents.vector: Exploitation of a vulnerability in BTCPay Server 2.4.1 and earlier, fixed in version 2.4.2 (August 2026), allowing theft from hot wallets.
incidents.impact: Bitcoin and Litecoin were stolen from hot wallets on outdated, internet-facing BTCPay Server instances; BTCPay urged affected operators to sweep funds and rebuild on fresh servers.

incidents.victim: Global Android TV and IoT device users (1.3M+ set-top boxes; 10M+ devices via affiliated malware)
incidents.attacker: Criminal gang — ad-fraud and residential-proxy botnet operation (device manufacturer Videostrong Technology Co., China-based)
incidents.vector: Device manufacturer Videostrong pre-loaded a backdoor ('x.cpe'/XCPE) into Android TV set-top boxes and other IoT devices, installed after first boot to evade Google's security testing.
incidents.impact: Backdoored devices were enrolled into ad-fraud, data-exfiltration and residential-proxy botnets; Google and partners took down the operators' infrastructure and banned the manufacturer from the Android ecosystem.

incidents.victim: U.S. Department of Defense (Pentagon network)
incidents.attacker: Unknown — accidental data exposure via contractor misconfiguration
incidents.vector: An Accenture employee connected an AI coding agent to a secure Pentagon system without authorization; the agent ran unsupervised on the network for two months.
incidents.impact: The agent exfiltrated controlled unclassified information (CUI) files and login credentials to a third-party website before the exposure was discovered.

incidents.victim: Michigan State University
incidents.vector: Suspected credential-compromise event detected in early October; a ransomware/extortion gang later claimed responsibility on its leak site.
incidents.impact: The gang claims to have stolen personal data on 1.3 million current and former students; the university says it found no evidence of a successful Active Directory compromise or data theft but required password resets campus-wide.

incidents.victim: Multiple airlines (Qantas, Japan Airlines, All Nippon Airways, Cathay Pacific, Malaysia Airlines, Korean Air) via the Amadeus reservation platform
incidents.vector: An intrusion at travel-reservation platform Amadeus in September exposed passenger data that cascaded to airline customers.
incidents.impact: Passenger data from multiple major airlines was exposed; additional carriers using Amadeus may be affected but have not yet disclosed breaches.

incidents.victim: CitySourced (government-technology platform) customers
incidents.vector: An unsecured database belonging to CitySourced was left online without a password.
incidents.impact: 42 million records were exposed and leaked online.

incidents.victim: cPGuard customers (cPanel / shared-hosting operators)
incidents.vector: An attacker used stolen credentials to access cPGuard's update servers and pushed a malicious update (versions 5.88.12-5.88.19) on November 2.
incidents.impact: The malicious update collected /etc/shadow files, MySQL configuration, root shell history, and SSH credentials from affected hosting servers before the vendor shipped a clean update.

incidents.victim: Mercado Bitcoin (Brazil's largest cryptocurrency exchange)
incidents.vector: Unspecified compromise of exchange infrastructure resulting in unauthorized withdrawal of crypto assets.
incidents.impact: Approximately $49 million in cryptocurrency was stolen; the exchange froze $11 million of the stolen funds and pledged to refund all affected users.

incidents.victim: Rosstat (Russia's state statistics service)
incidents.vector: Network intrusion by Belarusian and Ukrainian hacktivist groups, who claim to have first breached the agency roughly six months before disclosing it.
incidents.impact: Attackers claim to have stolen 23TB of data, including alleged state secrets, and to have wiped databases and internal systems.

incidents.victim: Software developers using the Cursor IDE / Claude Code extension (~5,000 systems)
incidents.vector: A malicious version of Anthropic's Claude Code extension was published to the Cursor VS Code Extension Marketplace, installing an attacker SSH key and persistence mechanism.
incidents.impact: Roughly 5,000 developer systems had SSH backdoors installed before Cursor pulled the extension and worked with a cloud provider to take down the attacker's command-and-control server.

incidents.victim: Ukraine (national air-raid alert system) and Russia (EMERCOM emergency alert system)
incidents.vector: Hackers breached Ukraine's official Air Alarm app to push fake Russian-language chemical/nuclear/street-fighting alerts for Kyiv; Ukraine retaliated by hacking Russia's EMERCOM system to send fake nuclear-strike alerts across 33 Russian regions.
incidents.impact: No sirens sounded and officials canceled both sets of fake alerts within minutes to hours, but the incidents show both sides' emergency-alert infrastructure remains exposed to hybrid-warfare disruption.

incidents.victim: Florida Department of Education
incidents.vector: Data was taken from a department website used by students to file for financial aid.
incidents.impact: Personal data belonging to 4.9 million students was stolen; the department says financial aid itself is not at risk.

incidents.victim: Binance
incidents.vector: A months-long social-engineering campaign (fake recruitment interviews, malicious developer tooling) compromised multiple employee devices, giving attackers access to wallet-signing and transaction-authorization systems.
incidents.impact: Roughly $6.34 billion in cryptocurrency was stolen within minutes; Binance has since recovered or replaced about 95% of customer losses from its own reserves, but hundreds of millions remain unrecovered and are being laundered.

incidents.victim: Space/satellite services, defense & aerospace technology, and policy-research organizations (multiple, unnamed)
incidents.vector: Exploited an authentication-bypass vulnerability (CVE-2026-20127) in Cisco SD-WAN Catalyst Controllers to deploy the custom 'KeyDrift' malware framework.
incidents.impact: KeyDrift intercepted decrypted SD-WAN control-plane traffic and exfiltrated IPsec keying material, providing long-term persistent access to victim networks for intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Six law firms (four in Canada, two in the U.S.)
incidents.vector: Believed to be the work of a ransomware/data-extortion gang that has specifically targeted U.S. and Canadian law firms over the past two years; intrusion method not disclosed.
incidents.impact: Six law firms disclosed security breaches in the same week, continuing a pattern of extortion attacks against the legal sector.

incidents.victim: Philippine Overseas Employment Administration
incidents.vector: An unidentified actor used privilege-escalation tools (GodPotato, SeImpersonate) and the Impacket library to copy 27 backup databases from a staging server in 24 minutes.
incidents.impact: Nearly 69GB of data on overseas workers, contracts, and financial/cashier records was exfiltrated; the stolen data has not yet appeared for sale, but researchers say it has value to both criminals and state actors.

incidents.victim: Government of Moldova
incidents.vector: Hackers breached government networks and began extracting data; IT staff detected the exfiltration in progress.
incidents.impact: Attackers stole personal information on roughly one-third of Moldova's population before officials shut down 82 public digital services and 30 government networks to contain the breach.

incidents.victim: Organizations running vulnerable PHP (WordPress/Drupal/Joomla sites; European government websites; a small fraction of internet-exposed Palo Alto Networks PAN-OS management interfaces)
incidents.vector: Two critical, unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP core (CVE-2026-109618, CVE-2026-109619, dubbed 'PHP2Shell') were exploited within hours of disclosure; one campaign chained the flaws with a Linux kernel privilege-escalation bug to gain root access, including against exposed PAN-OS management interfaces.
incidents.impact: Government websites in Europe went offline, and scanning/exploitation activity continued for weeks; Palo Alto Networks confirmed and individually notified the small number of customers affected through exposed management interfaces.
